properties.title: NRC Report: Emulsified Edible Oil Substrate (Eos 450) in South Ditch near Scott Afb, IL
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 925856 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: SAIC
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 925856
Incident Time: 2009-11-10 22:00:00
Nearest City: Scott Afb, IL
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: EMULSIFIED EDIBLE OIL SUBSTRATE (EOS 450)
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: SAIC
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 35 gallons
EMULSIFIED OIL SUBSTRATE (EOS) WAS BEING INJECTED INTO THE GROUND FOR REMEDIATION PURPOSES. INJECTIONS STARTED ON 8 NOVEMBER, AND SOUTH DITCH, WHICH FLOWS TO AN UNNAMED TRIBUTARY THAT FLOWS TO SILVER CREEK, WAS RUNNING WHITE. THIS WAS REPORTED TO THE BASE CIVIL ENGINEERING OFFICE 10 NOVEMBER, LATE IN THE DAY BY ANOTHER CONTRACTOR. A VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE DITCH TOOK PLACE 11 NOVEMBER. THE SOURCE WAS NOT DETERMINED UNTIL 16 NOV, AND WHEN WE WENT OUT TO LOOK AT THE DITCH THE DISCOLORATION WAS NO LONGER PRESENT. THE REMEDIATION CONTACT AT IEPA WAS CONTACTED LATER THAT DAY. GROUND INJECTIONS WERE COMPLETED BY 15 NOV.

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 10 feet by 300 feet (area 3000 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 42 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0.07 gallons
AT APPROXIMATELY 1600, AN EMPLOYEE FIELD OPERATOR WAS NOTIFIED BY A PUMPER FROM ANOTHER OIL COMPANY THAT THERE APPEARED TO BE A LEAK/SPILL NEAR ONE OF OUR PIPELINES. AFTER FURTHER INVESTIGATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE LEAK ORIGINATED FROM AN 8" STEEL LOW PRESSURE GATHERING LINE AND ITS CAUSE APPEARS TO BE FROM CORROSION. THE LEAK/SPILL OCCURRED IN AN UNNAMED TRIBUTARY OF WILDHORSE CREEK. APPROXIMATELY 1 BARREL OF HYDROCARBON SPILLED INTO CREEK. ACTION WAS TAKEN TO CONTAIN THE HYDROCARBON BY PLACING A SERIES OF THREE ABSORBENT BOOMS ACROSS THE CREEK APPROXIMATELY 300' DOWNSTREAM OF THE SPILL. THE LEAKING PIPELINE WAS CLAMPED TO STOP THE LEAK AND PREVENT ANY FURTHER LEAKAGE. FURTHER ASSESSMENT WILL BE MADE IN THE MORNING AND ADDITIONAL REMEDIAL MEASURES WILL BE TAKEN TO CLEAN UP SPILL.

properties.summary: Incident Type: STORAGE TANK - NRC Report ID: 797297 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: MOSIAC POTASH CARLSBAD INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 797297
Incident Time: 2006-05-11 19:00:00
Nearest City: Carlsbad, NM
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: HYDROCHLORIC ACID
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: MOSIAC POTASH CARLSBAD INC.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 3000 gallons
///WEB REPORT///37% HYDROCHLORIC ACID WAS BEING TRANSFERED WITHIN THE PLANT. THE OPERATOR WAS NOT AWARE OF A PIPING CHANGE. AS A RESULT, HE TOOK STEPS THAT CAUSED 3000 GALLONS OF ACID TO DRAIN INTO A CONCRETE CONTAINMENT. THE EMPLOYEES IN THE LOCATION DECIDED TO DILUTE THE ACID AND DRAIN IT TO THE TAILINGS AREA. MINE TAILINGS ARE THE WASTE CLAY AND SALT THAT REMAINS AFTER THE MINING PROCESS. THERE ARE SEVERAL MILLION TONS OF SLIGHTLY BASIC CLAY IN THE TAILINGS AREA. THE CLAY IMMEDIATELY NEUTRALIZED THE ACID. NO ADDITIONAL TREATMENT IS REQUIRED. THE SUPERVISOR REPORTED THE SPILL TO THE COMPANY EHS DEPARTMENT THE FOLLOWING DAY (MAY 12). THE EHS MANAGER WAS TRAVELING AND DID NOT RECEIVE THE NOTIFICATION UNTIL MAY 15. THE STATE AND FEDERAL RESPONSE CENTERS WERE NOTIFIED IMMEDIATELY AT THAT POINT.
